means:
Basic and undeveloped — limited to the first, crudest stage of something. Also, in biology, an organ or limb that never developed properly (*rudimentary wings*).

Watch the sting in it. **Fundamental** praises: it means essential, load-bearing, the thing everything rests on. **Rudimentary** faintly damns: it means *that's all there is so far*, and it isn't much. A rudimentary grasp of Mandarin gets you a taxi ride, not a conversation; a rudimentary shelter keeps some of the rain off. The word concedes that a thing exists while denying it is any good.
trick_line: **Rudi**mentary hides **rude** — in its old sense: rough, unfinished, knocked together.
trick_unpack: A "rude hut" wasn't impolite, it was crude — and that roughness is exactly what *rudimentary* still carries.
sentences: Excavation revealed a **rudimentary** drainage system: two stone channels and a sloped floor, nothing more.
My cooking skills are pretty **rudimentary** — I can do eggs and I can do toast.
etymology:
Latin **rudis** = *"rough, raw, unworked"* (of stone or timber), giving **rudimentum**, *"a first attempt, a beginning."*

Same root as **rude** (originally *unpolished*, only later *ill-mannered*) — and, best of all, **erudite**: *e-* "out of" + *rudis*, someone who has been **polished out of the rough**. Rudimentary and erudite are opposite ends of one root.
one_line: Basic and undeveloped — the crude first stage, nothing more.
